composition: Merge identical shared artifacts only, reject conflicting definitions, resolve Python module and symbol imports, preserve required package initializers, and require native realization coverage for every graph node. sources: Use the compiler-bundled domain contracts, exact Python strict profile and reference-factory contract. Preserve all predecessor capsule bytes. Bind selected source identities into the plan; do not read mutable development files during generation.
evidence: Native AST/import and positive/hostile behavior are required separately from deterministic planning. A registered plan is not proof of semantic qualification or release readiness.
staging: This candidate implements the whole-project generator join. Cross-project composition adapters, existing public source/snapshot/node/project/build command wiring, application output and verification must be completed before R10 qualification; unsupported staged paths fail explicitly, never silently fall back.
effects: Planning and artifact selection are non-effectful. No native process, filesystem publication, provider execution, admission, activation or default CLI cutover.
